source_text.body:
Extract change-of-control clauses from NDAs and draft legal memos
A lawyer runs Claude Code locally on his files to build a script pulling change-of-control clauses from 47 NDAs, and to draft memos and a junior associate guide.
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
An M&A lawyer ran Claude Code locally on a folder of files, so client documents never left his hard drive. He asked it in plain English to draft a script pulling change-of-control clauses from 47 NDAs into a spreadsheet with deal name, clause text and notes on unusual provisions. For memos, he did the research and saved the cases himself. Claude then drafted the memo from them.
How it went
The script took about 12 minutes to draft and 6 more to refine the prompt. In a separate 53-contract review, about 92% of clauses were right on the first pass, and he fixed the rest himself.
Worth knowing
Never let it generate citations; he sources cases himself and verifies all output before signing, treating it like a first-year associate's draft.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I have a folder of [number] contracts at [folder path], such as NDAs. Write and run a script that finds the [clause type, e.g. change-of-control] clause in each one and saves the results to a spreadsheet with columns for file name, clause text, and page or section. Then flag any files where no clause was found or where you are unsure, so I can check them by hand. Work on copies only and do not modify or delete my original files.
Original source: https://counsel-and-code.com/posts/im-a-lawyer-who-uses-claude-code-daily/
